To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the apparent gastrointestinal absorption (i.e. apparent retention in digesta) of methionine (MET), a sulfur amino acid (SAA), and 2-hydoxy-4-methythio-butanoic acid (HMTBA), a SAA precursor, were studied in conventional pigs and gnotobiotis (germ-free) pigs.
the bioavailability of methionine is lower than the bioavailability of MHA- FA in the pig.

(1) microbial metabolism of MTHF in the small intestine of pigs contributes, in part to its lower bioefficay compared to methionone and (2) the presence of commensal bacteria in the gut of pigs increases apparent absorption of MTHF compared to methionione.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of commensals on the apparent absorption of methionin and 2-hydoxy-4-methyithiobutanoate acid from the gastrointestinal tract.
the effect of commensals and diet composition on the apparent absorption of methionin and its metabolites.
the effects of the commensal microbial population on the bioavailability of methionine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbial metabolism of MTHFA increases retention in digesta relative to that of methionine.

methionine and its methylthio analogues are not significantly affected in the presence of a microbial community in the small intestine, but that the methylthio analogs have a lower apparent absorption than methionine.

microbial metabolism of methionine is more rapid and extensive in conventional compared to gnotobiotic piglets and that this is reflected in the lower bioavailability and apparent absorption of methionin
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence or absence of a microbiota does not affect apparent absorption of methionone or MHA-MA in the pig, but that diet composition and the presence or absence a microbiota does affect the microbial metabolism of MHTA-FA.
methionine is not metabolized to MHA-4FA in the small intestine of conventional pigs.
methionine is not metabolized by the microbiota, whereas MHA-FA is.
The main takeaway from our work is that
